response.rationale: Severe acute upper GI bleeding with hemodynamic instability, anemia, negative H. pylori/coagulation/infection workup, and persistent hemoglobin drop without CT-demonstrated active bleeding favors an occult bleeding source such as a vascular anomaly, best identified by early endoscopy.

rejected.why: Gastritis could cause coffee-ground vomiting, but the severe persistent bleeding and negative H. pylori/NSAID/infection workup are less supportive than a structural vascular lesion.
Peptic ulcer disease is contradicted by negative H. pylori testing and absence of NSAID use; no supportive ulcer-specific evidence is supplied.
Gastroesophageal varices are unlikely with normal liver function tests, no portal hypertension signs, and normal abdominal imaging.
Mallory-Weiss syndrome typically follows retching/vomiting and usually causes fresh hematemesis; no preceding retching is described.
